title: The Subjectivity of Monoculture
abstract: arXiv:2602.24086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Machine learning models---including large language models (LLMs)---are often said to exhibit monoculture, where outputs agree strikingly often. However, we present two experiments that substantially disagree with prior findings of monoculture. In particular, we find that monoculture virtually disappears in one dataset when we include item difficulty compared to previous works that do not.   Informed by these findings, we theoretically formalize what it means to measure monoculture. We show that monoculture is inherently subjective, relying on two key decisions: 1) the baseline null model for what "independence" should look like; and 2) the population of models and items under consideration. We conclude with concrete guidelines for future evaluators to ensure the robustness of their results.

translated_abstract: 机器学习模型——包括大语言模型（LLMs）——常被认为表现出“单一文化”现象，即它们的输出结果惊人地频繁一致。然而，我们提出了两个实验，其结果与先前关于单一文化的发现有重大分歧。特别是，我们发现，与之前未考虑条目难度的工作相比，当我们将条目难度纳入考量时，单一文化现象在某个数据集中几乎消失。基于这些发现，我们从理论上形式化了测量单一文化的含义。我们证明单一文化本质上是主观的，它依赖于两个关键决策：1）用于定义“独立性”应呈现何种形态的基线零模型；2）所考虑的模型与条目的总体范围。最后，我们为未来的评估者提供了具体的指导方针，以确保其结果的稳健性。
tldr: 本文通过实验与理论分析表明，机器学习模型“单一文化”现象的测量本质上是主观的，取决于对独立性基线零模型和模型与条目总体的选择，并为稳健评估提供了具体指导方针。
en_tdlr: This paper shows, both experimentally and theoretically, that measuring "monoculture" in machine learning models is inherently subjective, depending on the choice of the baseline null model for independence and the population of models and items, and offers concrete guidelines for robust evaluation.
